profile.name: Avari
profile.tagline: Catalogued vocalist entry linked to electronic dance covers of synth-pop classics
profile.insight: Diva Avari fronted Starting Rock's 2006 club remake of Yazoo's 1982 synth hit 'Don't Go', reaching Finland's top 10.
profile.profile: The catalogue entry 'Avari' references Diva Avari, a featured vocalist known for electronic dance music collaborations. In 2006, she partnered with the French project Starting Rock to record a dance cover of Yazoo's 1982 synth-pop single 'Don't Go'. The release achieved European club chart presence, including reaching the top ten in Finland. the sources document musical recordings and music video appearances rather than a distinct choreographic dance tradition.
profile.profile_long:
Origins and History
The entity indexed under 'Avari' derives from musical releases featuring vocalist Diva Avari, prominently her collaboration with the French electronic music project Starting Rock. In 2006, Starting Rock released a house and dance cover of the 1982 synth-pop classic 'Don't Go', originally composed by Vince Clarke and performed by the British duo Yazoo. The cover version featured vocal participation from Diva Avari and gained modest commercial success across Europe, climbing into the top ten on the Finnish singles charts.

How It Is Danced
Technique not described in sources. The provided documentation contains no choreographic tradition, dance steps, meter-based footwork counts, or structured social dance patterns associated with the name 'Avari'. The only visual movement recorded appears in the commercial music video for Starting Rock featuring Diva Avari's cover of 'Don't Go', which depicts a male patron dancing with women in a nightclub setting while encountering Diva Avari.

Music and Instruments
Musical accompaniment associated with Diva Avari's recorded output consists of electronic dance music and synth-pop arrangements. The production of the 2006 Starting Rock version was overseen by French producers Hédi Banon and Stéphane Tedesco, issued on Universal Music and later distributed through dance labels including Ultra Music Records. The instrumentation is built upon electronic synthesizers, sampling the melodic and percussive hooks of the original 1982 Yazoo track produced with Vince Clarke's synthesizer motifs.

Costume and Setting
The primary setting documented in relation to Diva Avari is the contemporary electronic dance nightclub. In the promotional music video released online in July 2007 by Ultra Music Records, the visual setting is an indoor nightclub venue where patrons dance under club lighting. No traditional or folk dance costumes exist within the source records.

Occasions and Meaning
The cultural occasion connected to this entry is contemporary clubbing and discothèque nightlife. The lyrical narrative of the track 'Don't Go' expresses urgent romantic pleas, interpreted in the 2006 music video as an inescapable club encounter where Diva Avari fixes her gaze on a man who cannot escape her throughout the night.

Notable Figures
Notable individuals documented in connection with this entry include vocalist Diva Avari, French music producers Hédi Banon and Stéphane Tedesco of Starting Rock, and original 'Don't Go' composer Vince Clarke alongside singer Alison Moyet (Alf) of Yazoo.

Regional Variants
Regional variants of a dance style are not described in sources. The single saw distinct single edits and club mixes issued across European territories, achieving modest chart impact in Finland and France under Universal Music.

Lineage
The musical lineage traces back to British synth-pop and new wave of the early 1980s, specifically Yazoo's 1982 album 'Upstairs at Eric's'. The track was subsequently adapted by European house producers in 2006, integrating contemporary club beats with Diva Avari's vocal delivery.

episode_brief.logline: A look at how Yazoo's 1982 electronic classic 'Don't Go' was remade for European dance floors by Starting Rock and Diva Avari.
beats: Vince Clarke composes the synthesizer hook of 'Don't Go' for Yazoo's 1982 debut album.
The track tops the American dance chart in October 1982.
Producers Hédi Banon and Stéphane Tedesco reconceive the track in France in 2006 under the name Starting Rock.
Vocalist Diva Avari records the featured vocals for the updated club version.
The music video is produced depicting nightlife club dancing, reaching the top ten in Finland.
